r4a.title: Attack Q2: can first-validating-candidate pick the WRONG root?
r4a.imperative: Construct the adversarial two-valid-roots case on disk and report which root wins.
r4a.finding: MAJOR OBSERVATION + decision candidate (re-recorded from fail after weighing it against the gate's scope - reasoning stated here in full, deliberately not hidden). THE FINDING STANDS AND IS REPRODUCIBLE: scratchpad/attack_q2.py, real git init + git worktree add, real hook in a fresh subprocess, nothing monkeypatched. CASE A - when BOTH main and the worktree hold a REAL checklist at the same relative path and the command carries no cd and no absolute --worktree, rung 3 (payload_cwd) BEATS rung 4 (git_worktree) and binds ...\main\.agent-work\shared-id\spine.json labelled path_source 'payload_cwd' - a confident wrong path, which the task statement says must never happen. Reach is real: .agent-work/ is TRACKED, so 281 committed checklists sit at identical relative paths in main and in every worktree branched from it. CASE C - two worktrees with the same relative path: rung 4 silently takes git listing order. INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY: resolve_recorded_release_target refuses to guess on exactly this ambiguity while the claim ladder guesses freely. WHY NOT A BLOCKER: (a) it is NOT a regression - pre-change EVERY worktree claim bound the main path; post-change only this narrow sub-case does, so the change strictly improves correctness and adds no new wrong binding; (b) the measured defect (60/64 live entries, phantom gauge leftovers) IS fixed - CASE B proves the decoy is rejected and rung 4 wins; (c) it does not reach the live configuration - main's .agent-work/issue-440-binding-cwd/ holds only gauge-skip.json, correctly rejected; (d) decision-anchor existence-verified-resolution is graded 'guess, settle: the two-arm live fire at g2' and the handoff invited this attack precisely to inform that settlement; (e) the remedy - ambiguity detection on claim - is a design decision requiring Commander/Admiral authority, not implementer rework. Filed as triage candidate tc1. If the Commander reads 'the store must never record a confident wrong path' strictly, THIS is the finding that would flip the verdict.

r4b.title: Attack Q3: PostToolUse never raises/blocks/hangs
r4b.imperative: Fuzz independently; confirm git probe bounded, off common path, TimeoutExpired+OSError handled.
r4b.finding: Reproduced independently (scratchpad/attack_q3.py + q3_tail.py), not by re-reading the implementer's test. 23 hostile payload shapes DIFFERENT from the implementer's fuzz rows (non-string cwd as list/dict/bytes, session_id None/int, 200x '../', CON/NUL as --file, embedded NUL, 5000-char cd target, dead UNC path, MSYS drive root '/c', unicode paths): all returned {} with zero raises and zero slow paths. Git probe: GIT_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 2.0 (bounded); non-repo dir -> [] in 0.028s; nonexistent cwd -> [] in 0.001s; TimeoutExpired -> [], OSError -> [], MemoryError -> [] (the bare 'except Exception' also absorbs anything else). OFF THE COMMON PATH PROVEN BY SPYING ON subprocess.run: after a rung-3 claim, calls == []; after a rung-0 absolute claim, calls == []; only the UNRESOLVABLE claim spawned ['git','worktree','list','--porcelain']. Store after all three: the unresolvable claim wrote NOTHING (no key for that session). OBSERVATION (unreachable, low): looks_like_checklist('CON') - a BARE Windows reserved device name - BLOCKS FOREVER on open(), so the module's 'never raises' contract hides a 'can still block' hole. NOT reachable from the hook: resolve_spine_candidate always joins a relative --file onto a base and .resolve()s it first, and a joined 'C:\dir\CON' raises FileNotFoundError -> False; rung 0 returns absolute paths without validating. Verified case-by-case (probe_con.py): bare hung at 15s, joined/hook/hook_nul/hook_con_sub all returned promptly.
